entries.title: Jeremiah 13:5
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: So - Most think Jeremiah did this in a vision, for it was a very long journey from Anathoth to Euphrates.

entries.title: Jeremiah 13:12
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Do we not know - This is no strange thing.

entries.title: Jeremiah 13:13
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Behold - There is a wine of astonishment and confusion, Psa 60:3. With that wine, saith God, I will fill all orders of persons, kings, priests, prophets, and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem.

entries.title: Jeremiah 13:16
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Give glory - Glorify God, by an humble confession of your sins, by submitting yourselves to God, humbling yourselves under his word, and under his mighty hand, before God brings upon you, his great and heavy judgments.

entries.title: Jeremiah 13:19
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: The cities - The cities of Judah lay southward from Chaldea.

entries.title: Jeremiah 13:20
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Where - The prophet speaks to the king, or to the rulers. In the multitude of the people is the king's honour.

entries.title: Jeremiah 13:21
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: What wilt thou say - Thou wilt have nothing to say, but be wholly confounded when God shall visit thee with this sore judgment, for by thy so often calling them to thy assistance, thou hast taught them to be captains over thee.

entries.title: Jeremiah 13:22
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Thy skirts - Probably these phrases are fetched from the usual practice of soldiers when they have conquered a place and taken prisoners, to strip them. By skirts is meant the lower part of their bodies covered with the lower part of their garments.

entries.title: Jeremiah 13:26
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Therefore - I will expose thee to shame and contempt.
